text.en: Social withdrawal: Reduced interest in and attention to others. Associated with reduced social interactions, and reduced time spent with others.

definition.en: Reduced interest in and attention to others. Associated with reduced social interactions, and reduced time spent with others.

probes.en: Have you had less interest in spending time with other people, including your family members, friends, or persons you work with?
Did you actually spend less time interacting with others?
How much less time than usual for you does this represent?
Did you avoid social contact with people whom you normally interact with?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight reduction in interest in social interaction
Mild; e.g., actual reduction in social interaction, associated with some avoidance of others
Moderate; e.g., substantially reduced time spent with others, with some adverse consequences to the social avoidance
Marked reduction in social interactions, with consequent difficulties in relationships with family, friends, peers

text.en: Reduced sex drive: Reduced sexual interest, fantasies, or a reduction of sexual activity. Judge against the subject's usual sexual interests and habits when well.

definition.en: Reduced sexual interest, fantasies, or a reduction of sexual activity. Judge against the subject's usual sexual interests and habits when well.

probes.en: What has your sexual interest and activity been like this past week?
Has it been reduced at any time?
Can you tell me an example of the way it has changed, been low?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; sexual interest is reduced
Mild; e.g., definite reduction of sexual interest. Usual sexual activities partially reduced
Moderate; e.g., persistent reduction of sexual interest. Usual sexual activities reduced consistently
Severe; e.g., complete sexual indifference. "I have no interest in sex."

text.en: Anxiety - reported: Subjective feelings of anxiety, fearfulness, or apprehension, whether or not accompanied by somatic anxiety and whether focused on specific concerns or not.

definition.en: Subjective feelings of anxiety, fearfulness, or apprehension, whether or not accompanied by somatic anxiety and whether focused on specific concerns or not.

probes.en: Have you felt tense or anxious?
Does this get to the point that you feel uncomfortable?
Are you able to control these feelings?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., fleeting inner tension
Mild; e.g., periods of tension, fear that can be mastered
Moderate; e.g., tense, ill at ease most of the time, minimal ability to control tension, fear
Severe; e.g., tense, fearful, frequent anxiety attacks. Often functionally incapacitating

text.en: Anxiety - observed: Autonomic over-activity and/or muscle tension, expressed in facial appearance, flushing, sweating, cold hands, posture, movements.

definition.en: Autonomic over-activity and/or muscle tension, expressed in facial appearance, flushing, sweating, cold hands, posture, movements.

probes.en: Over the past week have others commented that you appeared tense or showed signs of anxiety, such as sweating or clammy hands?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; occasional or slight autonomic disturbances such as flushing or sweating under stress
Mild; e.g., autonomic disturbance on several occasions, even when not under stress
Moderate; e.g., tense, ill at ease most of the time, minimal ability to control tension, fear
Severe; e.g., tense, fearful, frequent anxiety attacks. Often functionally incapacitating.

text.en: Somatic anxiety - reported: Has been bothered by 1 or more physiological concomitants of anxiety.

definition.en: Has been bothered by 1 or more physiological concomitants of anxiety.

probes.en: Have you been bothered by physical symptoms like palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, headaches, stomach cramps, diarrhea or muscle tension?
If yes, determine if there were other symptoms and the overall severity of the disturbance.

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasionally palms sweat excessively
Mild; e.g., often has 1 or more physical symptoms to a mild degree
Moderate; e.g., often has several symptoms or 1 symptom to a considerable degree
Severe; e.g., very frequently bothered by 1 or more symptoms or 1 symptom to a severe degree
